items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I was playing with Duke Ellington, Harry Edison, and I played with Ray Brown.

ctx.x: Well, we have to all play together...

That's what I mean. Now once he plays with the bass fiddle it's like the heart, the lungs of the body, and then he goes and he plays. But the most gratifying thing, as we were speaking about the Yale thing, it was the greatest thing that personally I have ever had a chance to see, that I'm sitting up on the bandstand. I didn't get a chance to play with you. I was playing with Duke Ellington, Harry Edison, and I played with Ray Brown. Ray Brown says, 'What am I playing?' And I said, 'Don't ask me; ask Duke…
They start from the bottom. Peoples like you or Charlie Mingus or Ray Brown or what have you, you are the basics of the academy of the music field.
